entities.name: PMID:25451401
observations: Fried and Nesse studied whether major depression presents as a consistent syndrome by examining unique symptom patterns in STAR*D participants.
Published in Journal of Affective Disorders 172:96–102; DOI 10.1016/j.jad.2014.10.010.
Accessible bibliographic records confirmed the citation, but did not expose the abstract or full text for independent verification of exact profile counts.

entities.name: Depression symptom heterogeneity
observations: The STAR*D investigation was designed to test consistency of depressive symptom configurations; its reported conclusion is that depression is not a consistent syndrome.
Distinct symptom combinations indicate heterogeneity of presentation, but profile diversity alone does not establish distinct diseases or invalidate depression as a clinically useful syndrome.
Exact numerical results should be checked against the primary article because they were not available in the retrieved abstract-level records.
